PullRequest.Title: Use synchronous hooks for ESM ASAR resolution
PullRequest.Body:
## Background

VS Code installs a custom ESM resolution hook in Electron processes to:

1. Map ESM `fs` imports to Electron's ASAR-unaware `original-fs`.
2. Resolve application bare package imports from `node_modules.asar`.
3. Prefer dependencies bundled closer to an importer.
4. Prevent resolution from escaping the application into an outer checkout's `node_modules`.

The hook currently uses Node's asynchronous `module.register`. Node runs those hooks on a dedicated loader worker, while static module linking synchronously waits for the worker.

This became visible while investigating Windows startup performance after Agent Host began prewarming during `WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore`. An Agent Host utility-process profile attributed:

- 149 ms to `node:internal/modules/esm/hooks#makeSyncRequest`
- 92 ms to ESM source compilation
- 64 ms to process spawn

Most `makeSyncRequest` time was the main Agent Host thread waiting synchronously for the loader worker during static module linking.

Node 24 provides `module.registerHooks`, which runs synchronous hooks in-process. VS Code already uses this API in the extension host.

## Change

Port the existing ASAR resolver to `module.registerHooks`.

Resolution behavior remains the same:

- ESM `fs` maps to `node:original-fs`.
- Bare packages first use default resolution so an importer's closer bundled dependency wins.
- A default resolution outside the application tree is rejected.
- Missing packages are looked up in `node_modules.asar`.
- Package self-reference resolution still applies real `exports`, `main`, and ESM import conditions.
- Packages without exports retain the direct, escape-proof archive fallback.
- Electron built-ins remain excluded.
- Resolution tracing through `VSCODE_ASAR_TRACE` remains available.

Synchronous hooks also apply to CommonJS resolution, unlike asynchronous hooks. The resolver therefore explicitly bypasses contexts containing the `require` condition, preserving existing `require()` and `createRequire()` behavior.

## Startup scenario improvement

The final A/B uses two fully bundled current-source Windows desktop applications:

- Same source revision
- Same official Electron runtime
- Same product/resources/extensions
- Same minification and NLS processing
- Complete `out/` directories differ only by this change

Each app received three warmups followed by 30 measured starts. Every individual start was interleaved, alternating A/B and B/A order. The standard performance scenario opens a deterministic local folder and one text file with extensions, updates, experiments, workspace trust, GPU, telemetry, and crash reporting disabled.

| Metric | Baseline | Synchronous hook | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total startup | 1435.5 ms | 1420.5 ms | **-18.5 ms** |
| Bootstrap 95% interval | | | **-33.5 ms to -7.0 ms** |
| Main bundle load | 152.0 ms | 118.0 ms | **-33.5 ms** |
| Workspace service init | 54.0 ms | 43.5 ms | **-11.0 ms** |
| Storage init | 22.0 ms | 18.0 ms | **-4.0 ms** |

The phase measurements overlap and should not be summed. The conservative end-to-end startup win is 18.5 ms on this Windows host.

## Improvements to other scenarios

The same bootstrap is shared by Electron main/CLI and `bootstrap-fork` processes such as Agent Host, extension host, shared/process services, file watchers, and terminal hosts.

Measured improvements in the packaged A/B:

| Scenario | Baseline | Synchronous hook | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Agent Host start to protocol connect | 962.5 ms | 759.0 ms | **-203.0 ms** |
| Shared-process connection | 518.0 ms | 420.5 ms | **-98.0 ms** |
| Extension registration | 761.5 ms | 734.5 ms | **-20.0 ms** |

Agent Host launch timing relative to workbench startup is unchanged (+4 ms, interval includes zero), while protocol connection becomes substantially faster. This preserves the early prewarm behavior required by #324330 rather than moving work after startup.

The packaged CLI also starts successfully through the synchronous hook.

## Compatibility / lack of regressions

Validation covered the behavioral differences between asynchronous and synchronous Node hooks:

- Direct packaged assertion:
  - ESM `import('fs')` resolves to `original-fs`.
  - CommonJS `require('fs')` remains the normal Electron/Node module.
- Packaged GUI standard startup succeeds.
- Packaged CLI `--version` succeeds.
- Packaged Agent Host resolves ASAR dependencies, connects, and lists sessions.
- No module resolution errors in correctly bundled baseline/fix runs.
- Agent Host launch is not deferred.
- Production desktop bundling succeeds.
- Client typecheck succeeds.

Tests:

```text
AgentHostPrewarmContribution and LocalAgentHostService: 19 passing
Agent Host diff worker: 6 passing
```

The diff-worker coverage is relevant because synchronous hooks are process-local and are not inherited by worker threads; the existing worker imports only built-ins/internal files and continues to pass.

Two independent implementation/diff reviews found no significant correctness or compatibility issue.

## Commands

```text
npm run typecheck-client
node build\next\index.ts bundle --minify --nls --target desktop --out perf-test\cache\bundle-sync-hook-pr
scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\agentHost\test\electron-browser\agentHostService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\electron-browser\localAgentHostService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\diffWorkerMain.test.ts
```

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The asynchronous ESM resolver ran on Node's loader worker, forcing the importing thread to issue and synchronously wait for a cross-thread hook request for each module-resolution edge during cold process startup.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Packaged Electron process startup accumulated loader-worker wait latency across the ESM graph; the supplied profile attributes 149 ms to makeSyncRequest in Agent Host, and the interleaved packaged A/B reports lower end-to-end desktop and child-process startup times after removing the boundary.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Registers the ASAR resolver in-process with synchronous module hooks, eliminating the loader-worker request/response boundary while keeping package resolution on the same module-linking critical path and preserving resolution cardinality.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, bootstrap-esm.ts imported module.register and registered a data-URL loader whose resolve hook was async and awaited nextResolve. Every Electron entrypoint imports this bootstrap before dynamically importing its main ESM graph (src/main.ts startup, src/bootstrap-fork.ts, src/cli.ts, and server entrypoints), so Node had to synchronously rendezvous with the dedicated loader worker during static linking for each resolution. The PR replaces that registration at RIGHT line 97 with module.registerHooks and a synchronous resolve callback while preserving the same default and ASAR resolution operations. The PR's profiled packaged A/B reports makeSyncRequest time on the old path and lower desktop, Agent Host, shared-process, and extension-registration startup latency with the changed hook.

Scenarios.Scenario: Packaged desktop cold startup through src/main.ts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: bootstrap-esm installs the resolver before startup dynamically imports the Electron main graph, so hook execution and package resolution must finish before the main bundle can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The changed implementation resolves in-process; the base module.register implementation sent each ESM resolution to Node's loader worker and synchronously waited for its reply.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one loader-worker rendezvous for each ESM resolution handled during cold linking; now zero. Module caching avoids relinking already-loaded modules within the process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The async data-URL hook ran on the loader worker and each main-thread static-link request waited for completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The old rendezvous serialized on static module linking; the diff removes it from startup's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Node default package lookup, archived package.json lookup, and package self-reference/direct ASAR resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One default lookup per relevant bare resolution; only failed or escaped default lookups continue to the archived package and self-reference/direct lookups. Effective work is bounded by the cold ESM graph and Node's module/resolution caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The async hook performed the same default, archive package.json, self-reference, and direct fallback sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These lookups remain on module linking's critical path, but the PR does not increase their count or add a new filesystem operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of uncached bare-specifier resolution edges in the startup ESM graph; each new desktop process has a cold module cache, while OS filesystem caches may be warm.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Static ESM linking waits for resolution. The old implementation serialized through loader-worker requests; the new callback runs synchronously in-process.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Node's module cache prevents repeated evaluation within a process; a fresh process starts cold. The resolver adds no persistent cross-process cache, before or after the change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: entrypoint ordering, hook type, and the unchanged resolution sequence are directly visible in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact savings vary by platform, graph shape, and OS cache warmth, but the removed per-resolution boundary and critical-path reachability are explicit; supplied packaged A/B data shows an end-to-end improvement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff removes loader-worker boundary fan-out and records a concrete startup regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron bootstrap-fork service startup for Agent Host, extension host, watcher, shared/process services, and terminal host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each spawned service executes bootstrap-fork, awaits bootstrapESM, then imports its selected ESM entrypoint; resolution therefore gates service readiness and protocol connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launches a dedicated Electron/Node child or utility process that runs bootstrap-fork.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per requested service instance; this launch count and scheduling are unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same services launched the same bootstrap-fork process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Process creation remains on service-start critical paths but is not introduced or moved by this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Per-process ESM resolution now executes in-process instead of crossing to a loader worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero loader-worker requests after the change versus one per handled ESM resolution in each cold child process before it; costs scale across both module graph size and concurrently starting services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every process independently registered the async worker hook and paid its worker rendezvous during linking.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removal shortens the path from process launch to imported entrypoint readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Default and ASAR-backed package resolution in each process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by each process's uncached bare ESM resolution graph, with archive fallback only after default resolution misses or escapes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical lookup sequence executed in the asynchronous resolver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still required before service entrypoint imports complete; operation count is preserved.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of independently started services multiplied by each service's cold ESM graph size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Several services may start concurrently, but each process performs synchronous module linking independently. No new burst or limiter change is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Module caches are process-local, so each child starts cold; warm OS disk caches can reduce filesystem latency but do not remove the old worker rendezvous.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: bootstrap-fork ordering and multiple concrete process starters are present in the repository.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact set and overlap of concurrently launched services varies by workspace and features, but the per-process path is certain and supplied measurements show improved service readiness.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; the removed worker boundary benefits each service without increasing subprocess or filesystem fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Packaged CLI and remote server startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CLI and server loaders await bootstrapESM before importing their main ESM implementation, so resolver work gates command output or server readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve packaged dependencies from closer node_modules locations or node_modules.asar.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per uncached relevant bare import, with archive fallback only on a default miss or out-of-app result; unchanged from the base implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same filesystem resolution algorithm ran in the async loader hook.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution remains blocking for startup, while the worker messaging layer is removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Eliminates Node loader-worker communication for ESM hooks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously scaled with handled ESM resolutions in each CLI/server process; now zero such cross-thread calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Async module.register required loader-worker dispatch and response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed from the command/server startup critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold CLI/server ESM graph size and number of independently launched commands/server processes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each process links modules synchronously; independent invocations can overlap at the OS level, unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fresh process module caches are cold; OS caches can be warm. No changed application cache or negative-cache behavior exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from cli.ts, server-cli.ts, and server-main.ts bootstrap-before-import ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CLI/server graph sizes differ by command, but the changed boundary direction is consistently favorable.

Scenarios.Scenario: CommonJS require and createRequire calls after bootstrap registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous hooks also observe CommonJS resolution, but the added callback classifies the context and immediately delegates before fs remapping or ASAR ESM fallback logic.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delegates to Node's existing CommonJS resolver, which may perform filesystem lookup on require-cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One delegation per CommonJS resolution hook invocation; underlying filesystem work and require-cache miss cardinality are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: CommonJS called Node's resolver directly and performed the same lookup; it did not traverse the async ESM hook.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new hook adds only condition checks before the same resolver. It does not add filesystem calls or move them onto a new path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of CommonJS resolution attempts after hook registration; packaged bundles and Node's require cache reduce effective cache-miss cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: CommonJS resolution is synchronous on each process thread; no new concurrency or queue is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful CommonJS modules remain cached by Node. The hook does not defeat that cache or retain per-specifier state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added interception and immediate bypass; low for any user-visible adverse magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The callback adds small CPU overhead per resolution, but no evidence establishes material latency against the removed ESM worker cost, and the packaged A/B results are favorable.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not reportable: constant classification overhead is real but no concrete performance regression is established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opt-in ASAR resolution tracing to a file
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When VSCODE_ASAR_TRACE names a file, trace lines are appended synchronously during module resolution and therefore gate traced startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per emitted trace line across relevant resolutions; the number and placement of trace calls are materially unchanged from the base hook.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old hook used appendFileSync for the same opt-in file sink and emitted equivalent per-resolution trace records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Writes remain blocking before a resolution returns. Previously the loader worker performed them while the importing thread waited; now they execute directly in-process.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of trace messages generated by the cold module graph; disabled by default.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Writes are synchronous within each process; multiple traced processes can write concurrently as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No trace cache exists. Normal module caching bounds resolution events within a process; each process opens/appends independently.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the old and new trace implementations in the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tracing can be expensive, but it is explicitly opt-in and the diff neither introduces the writes nor increases their effective cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression because the synchronous file-I/O mechanism and event count predate the PR.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each of three condition cases starts an Electron-as-Node child and waits for it to exercise the hook before assertions complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawns a fresh Electron-as-Node process for each test condition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly three serial test subprocesses for default, require, and import condition cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test file and its subprocesses did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded test-suite runtime only; it is not reachable in product startup or runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates a temporary fixture, writes three modules, and removes the directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary directory, three writes, and one recursive cleanup per suite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No fixture I/O existed because the suite was absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded setup/teardown cost in tests only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed three test cases and three fixture files, independent of workspace or user data size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mocha executes these cases serially in the suite; each execFile is awaited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each child is a cold process; fixtures are reused across the three cases and deleted once.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the explicit loop and awaited execFile call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime depends on process-launch speed, but cardinality is fixed and isolated to tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No product performance finding; bounded test overhead is appropriate for integration coverage.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced desktop, forked-service, CLI/server, CommonJS, tracing, and test paths. No actionable performance regression was introduced. The synchronous hook removes per-resolution loader-worker boundary fan-out; existing package-resolution filesystem work and opt-in trace writes retain their prior cardinality. The only added recurring cost is a small CommonJS context classification before immediate delegation, with no added I/O or evidenced user-visible regression. Recorded the concrete startup regression fix against introducing commit 913d5cccc1a0e97311521e7791033ce9d5c2ef2f.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
